mechanism_narrative: A sustained four-week decline in WORKPLACES mobility reduces weekday commuter-linked footfall near offices and transit hubs, mechanically lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as fewer people pass through retail corridors on their commute.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -8.9 to -32.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline or staying flat, invalidating the commute-linkage mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses below a -65% baseline threshold, it signals active public-health restrictions or widespread risk-avoidance behavior that spills over to suppress discretionary retail visits within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises within two weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -65%, showing no transmission from transit restriction severity to retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous four-week decline in WORKPLACES and rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility jointly indicate a behavioral shift toward staying home that compounds beyond either series alone, producing a larger suppressive effect on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than either trend predicts in isolation.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell while RESIDENTIAL rose each week t-3w through t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no larger than what WORKPLACES alone would predict, indicating no interaction effect between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: During the summer outdoor season, sustained elevated PARKS activity substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks as households favor open-air leisure over shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -15% while RETAIL_REC continues falling
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded to -11.7 at t-1w before dropping again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even as PARKS stays elevated, showing no substitution effect between outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A breach of GROCERY_PHARM mobility below -5% sustained for two consecutive weeks indicates that public caution has spread even to essential shopping trips, foreshadowing a further near-term decline in discretionary RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped to -8.7 at t-0w after being positive at t-3w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further within one week after GROCERY_PHARM breaches -5% for two weeks, rejecting the essential-to-discretionary spillover mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Joint acceleration of decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a collapsing commute-linked activity chain where fewer people travel to and from work hubs, mechanically reducing retail footfall tied to those commute paths within two weeks, beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fell sharply between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over two weeks matches the magnitude predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES individually, showing no amplifying interaction between the two.

mechanism_narrative: If the current co-movement of falling RETAIL_REC with rising RESIDENTIAL persists under an active pandemic surge regime, risk-averse households will continue voluntarily withdrawing from retail and recreation venues, further lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.7 to 17.7 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC fell from -11.4 to -40.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated, indicating the surge-driven caution mechanism has decoupled from retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-over-week swings in PARKS exceeding 20 points reflect weather-driven mobility substitution that creates short-term noise rather than a persistent trend; as outdoor activity normalizes, RETAIL_REC is expected to rebound slightly within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-over-week change exceeds 20 points in either direction
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -31.6 to -28.1 to -11.7 to -35.7 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to fall within one week after a greater-than-20-point PARKS swing, rejecting the noise-and-reversion mechanism.
